The '''2020–21 Bundesliga''' was the 58th season of the [[Bundesliga]], Germany's premier [[Association football|football]] competition. It began on 18 September 2020 and concluded on 22 May 2021.<ref name="calendar">{{cite news |url=https://www.dfl.de/de/aktuelles/neuer-rahmenterminkalender-fuer-saison-2020-21-veroeffentlicht-bundesliga-und-2-bundesliga-starten-am-18-september/ |title=Neuer Rahmenterminkalender für Saison 2020/21 veröffentlicht – Bundesliga und 2. Bundesliga starten am 18. September |trans-title=New schedule for the 2020/21 season published – Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga start on 18 September |website=DFL.de |publisher=[[Deutsche Fußball Liga]] |date=10 July 2020 |access-date=10 July 2020 |language=de}}</ref> The season was originally scheduled to begin on 21 August 2020 and conclude on 15 May 2021,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dfl.de/de/aktuelles/rahmenterminkalender-fuer-die-saison-2020-21-veroeffentlicht/ |title=Rahmenterminkalender für die Saison 2020/21 veröffentlicht |trans-title=Framework schedule for the 2020–21 season published |website=DFL.de |publisher=[[Deutsche Fußball Liga]] |date=5 December 2019 |access-date=1 March 2020 |language=de}}</ref> though this was delayed due to postponement of the [[2019–20 Bundesliga|previous season]] as a result of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany|COVID-19 pandemic]]. The fixtures were announced on 7 August 2020.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.kicker.de/bayern_startet_gegen_s04_der_komplette_bundesliga_spielplan_2020_21_zum_durchklicken-781328/artikel|title=Bayern startet gegen S04: Der komplette Bundesliga-Spielplan 2020/21 zum Durchklicken|website=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|date=7 August 2020|access-date=7 August 2020|language=de}}</ref>

[[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] were the defending champions and successfully defended their title, winning their record-extending 9th consecutive title and 31st title overall (30th in the Bundesliga era) on 8 May with three games to spare.<ref>{{Cite news|date=8 May 2021|title=Bayern Munich crowned Bundesliga champions|url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/bayern-munich-crowned-german-champions-2020-21-lewandowski-flick-davies-15756|access-date=8 May 2021|publisher=Bundesliga}}</ref> By winning their thirtieth Bundesliga title, Bayern Munich are honoured with a fifth [[Star (football badge)|gold star on their team badges]] and shirts.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://media.dfl.de/sites/2/2021/03/Anhang-IV-zur-LO-2021-03-05-Stand.pdf |title=Anhang IV zur LO: Richtlinie für Spielkleidung und Ausrüstung |trans-title=Annex IV to the Licensing Regulations: Guideline for Match Clothing and Equipment |work=[[Deutsche Fußball Liga]] |page=19 |date=5 March 2021 |access-date=8 May 2021 |language=de |quote=Die Clubs, die seit 1963 in der Bundesliga eine bestimmte Anzahl von deutschen Meistertiteln errungen haben, sollen auf dem Trikot unmittelbar angrenzend an das Clubemblem als Titelsymbol einen oder mehrere Sterne nach den folgenden Maßgaben abbilden: ... e) Ab dreißig gewonnenen Meistertiteln: fünf Sterne. [The clubs that have won a certain number of German league titles since 1963 shall display one or more stars on the jersey immediately adjacent to the club emblem as a title symbol in accordance with the following requirements: ... e) From thirty championship titles won: five stars.]}} [https://megalodon.jp/ref/2021-0509-0112-02/https://media.dfl.de:443/sites/2/2021/03/Anhang-IV-zur-LO-2021-03-05-Stand.pdf Alt URL]</ref>

Bayern's [[Robert Lewandowski]] set a new record for goals scored in a season with 41, surpassing the previous record of 40 goals set by [[Gerd Müller]] in [[1971–72 Bundesliga|1971–72]].<ref name="Lewandowski 41">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57213750 |title=Bayern Munich 5–2 Augsburg: Robert Lewandowski breaks goalscoring record |work=BBC Sport |date=22 May 2021 |access-date=22 May 2021}}</ref>

==Effects of the COVID-19 pandemic==
On 3 September 2020, the [[Deutsche Fußball Liga|DFL]] General Assembly voted to extend the use of five substitutions in matches to the 2020–21 season, which was implemented at the end of the previous season to lessen the impact of fixture congestion caused by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dfl.de/de/aktuelles/beschluss-der-dfl-mitgliederversammlung-medizinisch-hygienisches-konzept-wird-statuarisch-verankert/ |title=Beschluss der DFL-Mitgliederversammlung: Medizinisch-hygienisches Konzept wird statuarisch verankert |trans-title=Resolution of the DFL General Assembly: Medical hygiene concept to be incorporated into the statutes |website=DFL.de |publisher=[[Deutsche Fußball Liga]] |date=3 September 2020 |access-date=3 September 2020 |language=de}}</ref> The use of five substitutes, based on the decision of competition organisers, had been extended by [[International Football Association Board|IFAB]] until 2021.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fifa.com/who-we-are/news/five-substitute-option-extended-into-2021-in-response-to-covid-19-pandemic |title=Five-substitute option extended into 2021 in response to COVID-19 pandemic |work=[[FIFA]] |date=15 July 2020 |access-date=3 September 2020}}</ref> Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the season began with matches [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] or at reduced capacity due to restrictions across German [[States of Germany|states]]. [[Leipzig]] allowed up to 8,500 spectators to begin the season, while regulations in [[Berlin]] allowed for up to 5,000 supporters.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.kicker.de/fan_rueckkehr_seifert_und_die_profi_klubs_sehen_keine_wettbewerbsverzerrung-783473/artikel |title=Fan-Rückkehr: Seifert und die Profi-Klubs sehen keine Wettbewerbsverzerrung |trans-title=Fan return: Seifert and the professional clubs see no distortion of competition |work=[[Kicker (sports magazine)|kicker]] |date=3 September 2020 |access-date=3 September 2020 |language=de}}</ref>

==Summary==
[[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] began the season less than a month after defeating [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] in the [[2020 UEFA Champions League Final|Champions League final]], as the match had been delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic. In their first game, they beat [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] 8–0, and were the dominant side early on in the season. After a 3–2 away victory over title contenders [[Borussia Dortmund]] in November, many pundits praised Bayern as the best team in Europe.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Whitebloom |first1=Grey |title=Bayern Munich Are Still the Best Team in Europe & it's Not Even Close |url=https://www.90min.com/posts/bayern-munich-are-still-the-best-team-in-europe-it-s-not-even-close |website=90min |access-date=11 May 2021 |date=22 October 2020 |archive-date=11 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210511194940/https://www.90min.com/posts/bayern-munich-are-still-the-best-team-in-europe-it-s-not-even-close |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Da Silva |first1=Michael |last2=Harding |first2=Jonathan |title=Breathless Bayern set new standards with Klassiker triumph |url=https://www.dw.com/en/breathless-bayern-set-new-standards-with-klassiker-triumph/a-55520158 |website=DW |access-date=11 May 2021 |date=7 November 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Sinnott |first1=John |title=Bayern Munich remains in a class of its own after 'Der Klassiker' triumph |url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/11/08/football/bayern-munich-borussia-dortmund-der-klassiker-spt-intl/index.html |website=CNN |access-date=11 May 2021 |date=8 November 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Betts |first1=Eric |title=Why Bayern Munich Is Steamrolling Europe's Soccer Titans |url=https://slate.com/culture/2020/12/bayern-munich-dominance-champions-league-bundesliga.html |website=Slate |access-date=11 May 2021 |date=4 December 2020}}</ref>  This praise continued all season long, with former Bayern manager [[Pep Guardiola]] proclaiming them the best club in Europe in March.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bayern, not Manchester City, are best club in Europe - Guardiola |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-soccer-england-mci-wlv-preview-idUSKBN2AT365 |website=Reuters |access-date=11 May 2021 |date=1 March 2021}}</ref> Bayern mathematically confirmed their ninth consecutive Bundesliga title on 8 May 2021 with three matches to spare, following closest contender [[RB Leipzig]]'s 2–3 loss to Dortmund.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bayern Munich win Bundesliga as Dortmund beat Leipzig |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57038735 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=11 May 2021 |date=8 May 2021}}</ref> The title was Bayern's 30th Bundesliga and 31st German championship overall, which would see them add a fifth [[Star (football badge)|star]] to their badge in the following season.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ford |first1=Matt |last2=Da Silva |first2=Michael |title=Bundesliga: Champions Bayern Munich hammer Gladbach after RB Leipzig defeat |url=https://www.dw.com/en/bundesliga-champions-bayern-munich-hammer-gladbach-after-rb-leipzig-defeat/a-57470633 |website=DW |access-date=11 May 2021 |date=8 May 2021}}</ref>

Meanwhile, Schalke 04 endured a disaster season, failing to win a game in nine consecutive months dating back to the previous season, before defeating a fourth-tier club in the [[DFB-Pokal|German Cup]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Schalke Ends Nine-Month Winless Streak |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2020/11/03/schalke-wins-dfb-pokal-ends-streak |magazine=Sports Illustrated |access-date=11 May 2021 |date=3 November 2020}}</ref>  They failed to win thirty Bundesliga matches in a row, falling one short of the all-time record set by [[SC Tasmania 1900 Berlin|Tasmania Berlin]] in [[1965–66 Bundesliga|1965–66]], before a 4–0 win against [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim|1899 Hoffenheim]] in January.<ref>{{cite web |title=Schalke end 30-game winless run to avoid unwanted Bundesliga record |url=https://www.thescore.com/deu_fed/news/2087881 |website=TheScore |access-date=11 May 2021 |date=9 January 2021}}</ref>  Schalke had announced before the season that they had debts of over 200 million, which led them to slash spending.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Penfold |first1=Chuck |title=Bundesliga: Schalke to slash spending, commit to coach David Wagner |url=https://www.dw.com/en/bundesliga-schalke-to-slash-spending-commit-to-coach-david-wagner/a-54013261 |website=DW |access-date=11 May 2021 |date=1 July 2020}}</ref> The poor results led to departures for executives and managers.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ford |first1=Matt |last2=Da Silva |first2=Michael |title=Bundesliga: Schalke 'tearing themselves apart' |url=https://www.dw.com/en/bundesliga-schalke-tearing-themselves-apart/a-53967463 |website=DW |access-date=11 May 2021 |date=18 December 2020}}</ref> Former Schalke star [[Klaas-Jan Huntelaar]] returned to Schalke from [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] in January in an attempt to stave off relegation, but he was unable to prevent Schalke from being relegated for the first time in over thirty years.<ref>{{cite web |title=Klaas-Jan Huntelaar returns to Schalke from Ajax |url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/klaas-jan-huntelaar-returns-to-schalke-from-ajax-14380 |website=Bundesliga |access-date=11 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Ford |first1=Matt |title=Schalke relegated from the Bundesliga: The inside story of a Royal Case of the Blues |url=https://www.dw.com/en/schalke-relegated-from-the-bundesliga-the-inside-story-of-a-royal-case-of-the-blues/a-57184763-0 |website=DW |access-date=11 May 2021 |date=21 April 2021 |archive-date=14 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210514174428/https://www.dw.com/en/schalke-relegated-from-the-bundesliga-the-inside-story-of-a-royal-case-of-the-blues/a-57184763-0 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

A hot start to the season for [[Robert Lewandowski]] led to early talk that he could break [[Gerd Müller]]'s 49-year-old record of 40 goals scored in one Bundesliga season, with teammate [[Thomas Müller]] suggesting it could happen back in October.<ref>{{cite web |title='Can't praise him enough': Mueller marvels at Lewandowski |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/news/ne4224484/ |website=WorldFootball.net |access-date=11 May 2021 |date=30 October 2020}}</ref> Lewandowski capped off a successful year in December by winning his first [[The Best FIFA Men's Player|FIFA Men's Player of the Year]] award.<ref>{{cite web |title=Best Fifa Football Awards 2020: Robert Lewandowski wins best men's player of the year |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/55354762 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=11 May 2021 |date=17 December 2020}}</ref> As Lewandowski continued his strong performances, interest in him overtaking Müller's record grew from various media outlets.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pearson |first1=Matt |title=Robert Lewandowski: The unbelievable Bundesliga stats |url=https://www.dw.com/en/robert-lewandowski-the-unbelievable-bundesliga-stats/a-56940030 |website=DW |access-date=11 May 2021 |date=20 March 2021}}</ref>  However, a knee injury suffered whilst on international duty on 31 March threatened Lewandowski's record-chase and kept him out of action for a month.<ref>{{cite web |title=Injury could rob Lewandowski of Müller record, fears former Bayern forward Roy Makaay |url=https://en.as.com/en/2021/03/31/football/1617192622_290488.html |website=AS |access-date=11 May 2021 |date=31 March 2021 |archive-date=11 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210511200730/https://en.as.com/en/2021/03/31/football/1617192622_290488.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>  Lewandowski returned to action in April, just five goals away from equalling the single-season goal record.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lewandowski set to resume chase for Gerd Mueller's record |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210421-lewandowski-set-to-resume-chase-for-gerd-mueller-s-record |website=France24 |access-date=11 May 2021 |date=21 April 2021}}</ref> On 15 May 2021, Lewandowski scored his 40th goal of the season against [[SC Freiburg]] with one match to spare, therefore equalling Gerd Müller's record tally from [[1971–72 Bundesliga|1971–72]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57129060 |title=SC Freiburg 2–2 Bayern Munich: Robert Lewandowski equals Gerd Muller's Bundesliga goals record |work=[[BBC Sport]] |date=15 May 2021 |access-date=15 May 2021}}</ref> In the last match of the season the following week, Lewandowski scored his 41st league goal in the final minute of the match against [[FC Augsburg]] to break Müller's record.<ref name="Lewandowski 41"/>
